title: Concurrent_MetateM
summary:
Concurrent MetateM is a multi-agent language in which each agent is programmed using a set of augmented temporal logic specifications of the behaviour it should exhibit. These specifications are executed directly to generate the behaviour of the agent. The root of the MetateM concept is Gabbay's separation theorem, which states that any arbitrary temporal logic formula can be rewritten in a logically equivalent past-implies-future form.

Execution proceeds by a process of continually matching rules against a history, and firing those rules when antecedents are satisfied. Any instantiated future-time consequents become commitments which must subsequently be satisfied, iteratively generating a model for the formula made up of the program rules.

The language uses two categories of temporal connectives. Strict past time connectives include weak last, strong last, was, heretofore, since, and zince (weak since). Present and future time connectives include next, sometime, always, until, and unless. A Concurrent MetateM system contains a number of concurrently executing agents, each of which is able to communicate with its peers via asynchronous broadcast message passing.

Concurrent MetateM represents a combination of the direct execution of temporal specifications together with a novel model of concurrent computation, and as such it provides a new approach to the modelling of complex reactive systems. Concurrent MetateM is a programming language created in 1993.
